figures.finding: Saint-Barthélemy's taxes are set by its Code des contributions, and it levies no personal income tax, so a resident of the island pays none on pay or fees.

sources.said: Les différents impôts et taxes perçus dans la collectivité sont prévus par le code des contributions de Saint Barthélemy. Il n'y existe ni impôt sur le bénéfice des sociétés ni impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques.

figures.finding: A person who moved to Saint-Barthélemy after 15 July 2007 is fiscally domiciled there only after five years' residence, and until then remains a French tax resident under France's income tax.

value.appliesTo: anyone not already resident of the island on 15 July 2007

sources.said: les personnes résidant à Saint-Martin ou à Saint-Barthélemy qui ont transféré leur domicile fiscal dans ces collectivités après le 15 juillet 2007 et qui ne remplissent pas la règle de domiciliation fiscale de cinq ans dans ces collectivités(2) … Sont considérées comme fiscalement domiciliées à Saint-Barthélemy les personnes physiques qui y ont résidé pendant cinq ans au moins. Cette disposition est applicable à toute personne ne possédant pas déjà la qualité de résidente de l’île.

figures.finding: In Saint-Barthélemy the Caisse de Prévoyance Sociale, run by MSA Poitou, collects social contributions; its 2026 table puts 13.00% employer health, 2.11% employer and 0.40% employee uncapped old-age plus 8.55% and 6.90% up to the ceiling, 5.25% family allowances, 4.00% employer unemployment up to four ceilings, and 9.20% CSG and 0.50% CRDS on 98.25% of pay, with the 2026 ceiling of 48,060 euros a year.

employee.name: CSG
employee.base: 98.25% of pay up to 4 ceilings, 100% above

value.selfEmployed: the CPS collects independent workers' contributions since 1 January 2020 (rates not published on the pages read)
value.dated: rates at 1 July 2026; ceiling at 1 January 2026

figures.applies: BL, 2026. The CPS Saint-Barthélemy publishes MSA's 2026 rate table, drawn up for the agricultural regime by reference to the Code de la sécurité sociale (D. 242-3, D. 242-4); no separate rate for a non-agricultural employer was found on its pages. The table says CSG and CRDS are due only from persons fiscally domiciled in France; whether a Saint-Barthélemy fiscal resident owes them is not stated there. Complementary pension (Agirc-Arrco), the intermittents' scheme and the self-employed rates are not modeled from these pages.
